data.body: Deep-dive research on ticket 4's Gerrit/CLI data flow revealed: render_findings_block (finding_publish.py) ALREADY shows no severity word per-finding today (only in the batch header via kind= param) -- so the Gerrit comment body already satisfies "no severity, blocking/advisory via structure" with zero code change needed there. The real defect worth fixing: adapter.py::_translate_findings flattens blocking+advisory into one list with NO field distinguishing which bucket a finding came from -- a genuine latent gap, fixable by adding blocking:bool there (replacing the never-rendered severity/_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY, which adapter.py computes but nothing downstream ever displays to a human). This surfaced a bigger question threatening ticket 6's scope: completion_reconcile.py hardcodes "severity": "high" independently of pass3_decide (a genuinely different, unrelated severity concept for DoD-failure findings, which never gets priority/decision and can't attain one within this epic) -- if ticket 6's planned removal of findings.py's SEVERITIES vocab/normalize_finding clamp is too broad, it could break completion_reconcile.py's and possibly other independent severity producers with no fallback signal, causing _render_verdict_text to print "?" for every completion-verdict finding. Dispatched exhaustive research enumerating every severity-setting producer in src/rebar/ before finalizing tickets 4 and 6 -- want to know definitively which producers are in-scope (pass3_decide-derived) vs which have their own independent severity concept that must survive.
